risks.title: Global Economic Uncertainty
risks.score_rationale: Uncertain global economic conditions, including high inflation, rising interest rates, labor shortages, and market volatility, directly impact consumer confidence and demand for the company's products in its key markets.

risks.title: Supplier Dependence
risks.score_rationale: The company's reliance on suppliers is highlighted, with potential risks related to the availability and pricing of raw materials.

risks.title: Increased Competition
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in competitive industries, including aerospace and defense, data center computing, and automotive, where quality standards are high and competition is intense.

risks.title: Foreign Exchange Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company is exposed to foreign exchange risks due to its multiple international operations (China, Malaysia, Canada) and holding capital in currencies other than the U.S. dollar.

risks.title: Dependence on a Few Customers
risks.score_rationale: In 2025, the top ten customers accounted for 55% of net sales, indicating high customer concentration and significant vulnerability to reduced demand from these major customers.

risks.title: Quality-Related Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company is subject to high quality standards, particularly in the aerospace and defense industry which represents 44% of sales, and a quality failure could have significant negative impacts on operating results.

risks.title: Production Capacity Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company must maintain adequate production capacity to meet growing demand in data centers and networking, and underutilized capacity could negatively impact operating results.

risks.title: Regulatory Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company is subject to strict government regulations, particularly regarding exports, imports, and national security requirements (ITAR, NISPOM), and regulatory changes could impact financial results.

ai_positioning.summary: TTM Technologies positions its investments in new production capabilities (Syracuse, Penang, Eau Claire) as supporting generative AI applications in data centers and networking, although AI is not a core strategic positioning for the company.
evidence: Syracuse facility: advanced technology capability for domestic high-volume production of ultra-HDI PCBs in support of national security requirements
Eau Claire facility: enhanced ability to support future high-volume U.S. production of advanced technology PCBs for generative AI applications
Penang facility: for commercial markets such as data center computing, networking, and medical, industrial markets
